instantiated_cells.justification: Ohio defines "legislative agent" by the qualitative "main purposes" test and requires registration within 10 days of any engagement for compensation; no minimum compensation dollar threshold is set.
Registration is triggered by engagement of a legislative agent within ten days, with no minimum expenditure dollar threshold required to trigger registration.
Itemized reporting of meals/food/beverages per official is required only when cumulative payments by the legislative agent during the calendar year to/for a particular official exceed a total of $50.

Each legislative agent and employer must file a statement of expenditures with each updated registration showing total expenditures during the reporting period; the statute imposes no dollar floor below which filing is excused.

The statute requires filing of updated registration and expenditure statements at fixed tri-annual deadlines regardless of any time-spent percentage, so no time-percent de minimis filing threshold exists.

arguments.justification: The statute defines "legislative agent" as an individual engaged "during at least a portion of the individual's time to actively advocate as one of the individual's main purposes" — a qualitative test with no numeric time-percentage threshold.

content.text:
I'll analyze the Ohio statute to answer each registration threshold question.

Key findings:
- §101.70(F): "legislative agent" = engaged to actively advocate "as one of the individual's main purposes" — no dollar or percent threshold, but qualitative "main purposes" test
- §101.72(A): Registration required within 10 days of engagement — no dollar threshold for registration itself
- §101.72(E): $25 registration fee (not a threshold)
- §101.73(B)(3): Itemization of meals/food/beverages required when total exceeds $50 per calendar year per official — this is the itemization de minimis threshold
- No overall expenditure dollar threshold for whether to file; statements must be filed with each updated registration regardless
- No numeric time percent — statute uses qualitative "main purposes" language
